conviction_note: The revenue line will very likely beat again: actual revenue has come in at or above the top of the company's own guide for four quarters running, and consensus sits at the midpoint. This stock has not paid for revenue beats (Q2 2026 beat the top of its guide by 6.7% and closed -1.1%; Q3 2025 beat consensus and fell 11.9% on an EPS miss). The fourth-quarter guide is exposed to diesel price rises in September and October and to slowing road freight, so print_vs_bar is about +3% but the reaction is close to a coin flip with a slight negative lean (p_up 47 on an abs move of 5).
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus is US$496.4M, about RMB3.37bn at the Q2 rate of 6.785 and so the midpoint of the company's RMB3.32-3.42bn guide. Consensus EPS is US$0.20 per ADS, about RMB1.33-1.36, with a whisper of $0.21. Sources: the company guide in the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/383529/full-truck-alliance-co-ltd-announces-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results, 2026-08-19); Earnings Whispers' preview (https://finviz.com/news/421317/full-truck-alliance-must-show-order-growth-can-hold-up-as-monetization-gains-mature, 2026-11-11); Benzinga's estimates page (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/YMM/earnings-forecasts, undated). Two estimate sources agree and the company guide also exists, so the bar is sourced. The Q4 2026 revenue consensus is about US$456.1M on Benzinga and is not confirmed by a second source.
positioning_check: Short interest was about 20.1M shares at the 2026-09-15 settlement, down 3.5M from the prior period, with 3.92 days to cover (FINRA via Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/ymm/short-interest). CurvedTrading reports 19.8M shares and 3.3 days at 2026-09-30 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/ymm/short-interest/). The tape reads -4.39% over 5 days and -1.47% over 20 days; the stock is 29% below its 52-week high and 11% above its low.

findings.finding: Revenue has landed at or above the top of the company's own guide four quarters in a row, and consensus sits at the midpoint of the current guide (about RMB3.37bn), so a revenue beat of roughly 2-6% is the base case. The record: Q4 2025 RMB3,192.6M against a 3.08-3.18bn guide; Q1 2026 RMB2,848.4M against 2.70-2.80bn; Q2 2026 RMB3,381.6M against 3.07-3.17bn, 6.7% over the top. The Q3 guide is RMB3.32-3.42bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not been rewarded. Q2 2026 beat the top of its guide by 6.7%; the stock opened about -6% at 8.27 and closed -1.1% (8.80 to 8.70, Yahoo chart). Q3 2025 beat revenue consensus (RMB3.36bn against 3.12bn) but missed EPS and fell 11.9% (12.32 to 10.85). Q4 2025, which landed just above its guide, closed -1.6%. Q1 2026, which beat the top of its guide by 1.7%, closed +4.3% and gave it back the next day.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at US$496.4M sits at the guide midpoint rather than near the top, which is where four quarters of history say revenue lands. If the market expected the usual beat, consensus or the whisper would sit at RMB3.45bn or more. But the beat pattern is public, and the stock has damped revenue beats, so only a small part of the beat is a price move.
findings.independence: The guide ranges come from separate releases: the Q1 2026 release with the Q2 guide (https://www.itiger.com/news/2637365594, 2026-05-22), the Q3 2025 release with the Q4 2025 guide (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/36155493/full-truck-alliance-co-ltd-announces-third-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results), and the Q4 2025 release (https://www.chartmill.com/news/YMM/Chartmill-44013-Full-Truck-Alliance-NYSEYMM-Reports-Mixed-Q4-2025-Results-Sees-Pre-Market-Gain). It is one company's own pattern, not an independent series.

findings.finding: China raised diesel prices twice in September 2026, actual increases of RMB250/t on Sep 11 and RMB385/t on Sep 24, as Brent touched about $109 on a US-Iran escalation. It raised them again on Oct 29 and cut RMB625/t only on Nov 12. The Q3 guide (Aug 19) was given when management credited 'consecutive diesel price cuts since June' with the recovery in order growth, and it had blamed high diesel for weaker low-value freight demand in Q2. That reverses one stated driver of order growth late in Q3 and through October, which weighs on September orders and the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on a diesel-driven guide. Order growth slowing from 14.3% to 12.7% (blamed on diesel) was met by a -6% open in Aug 2026 that recovered to -1.1%. The Q4 guide given in Nov 2025 came with a -11.9% day, though that day was driven by an EPS miss.
findings.why_not_priced: No sell-side preview found ties the Sep-Oct diesel reversal to YMM's order volume. The Earnings Whispers preview of Nov 11 frames order growth as the swing factor but cites only Q2's diesel and weather explanation. If it were priced, the Q4 revenue consensus would have been cut below the Q4 2025 base of RMB3.19bn and previews would name fuel. The stock's -4.4% over 5 days has no attributed cause.
findings.independence: Two separate sources: the Sep 11 hike (https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20260911/c679822768.shtml) and the Nov 12 cut, which followed an Oct 29 hike (https://www.news.cn/fortune/20261112/7ce2362ff2814b06a05934ed9ba0322e/c.html). Management's own link between diesel and orders is in the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15432330869752832). The transmission to YMM's Q3 and Q4 is an inference and the company has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Road freight growth slowed into the end of the quarter and freight rates were flat. Jan-Sep 2026 road freight was +2.5% YoY against +2.7% for Jan-Aug, which implies a soft September, and total September freight was +1.3%. The October road freight rate index was 104.9, -0.06% YoY, with the truckload index -0.03%, and capacity is described as persistently high. Heavy truck sales fell 10% YoY in September. This is a soft volume backdrop for fulfilled-order growth, which was 12.7% in Q2, and for the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The order-growth slowdown in Q2 (14.3% to 12.7%) closed -1.1% after a -6% open. Q4 2025's slowdown to 12.3% order growth, attributed to ecosystem governance, closed -1.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public macro series that are partly priced. YMM's own order growth has run far above road tonnage (12.7% against about 2.5%), so the transmission is weak. If the market fully priced a slowdown, consensus would not hold flat QoQ EPS. Oversupplied capacity can also lift YMM's fulfillment rate, which partly offsets.
findings.independence: The rate index is a separate CFLP/Lin'an series (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026110600030674, 2026-11-06). The heavy truck data is SteelOrbis (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/heavytrucksalesin-china-increase-by-13-percent-in-january-september-2026-1482511.htm). This is a proxy only; the company has not confirmed it. The October logistics PMI was 51.2, still expanding (https://www.news.cn/fortune/20261103/0ed4562bb56d446589888832b2b3e7eb/c.html), which partly offsets.

findings.finding: The earnings comparison is easy and the main driver of last year's Q3 miss is shrinking. Q3 2025 income from operations was only RMB776.3M, with adjusted EPS of RMB0.93 against a RMB1.08 consensus, hit by brokerage tax-related costs net of government grants. Since then brokerage revenue has fallen to RMB995M, the company has moved to an aggregator model that it says cuts VAT refund and settlement risk, and Q2 2026 income from operations rose 30.4% to RMB1,486M. The roughly RMB1.33-1.36 consensus is about flat QoQ and needs no repeat of the Q3 2025 cost spike.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS is the line this stock has traded on: the Q3 2025 EPS miss despite a revenue beat drove -11.9%, and the Q2 2026 EPS beat (RMB1.36 against 1.26) gave only -1.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus already embeds about +45% YoY EPS, so the recovery is in the bar. What the market may not be pricing is that the cost line behind last year's Q3 drop is structurally smaller. Grant timing is lumpy, though, so this is small and two-sided.
findings.independence: The brokerage transition and the VAT-risk statement come from the Q2 2026 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15432330869752832), a different document. The Q2 operating income figure is from the Q2 release.

findings.finding: Credit quality is worsening in the value-added services line. The NPL ratio rose to 3.8% from 2.9% at end-2025, partly on a methodology change that now includes off-balance-sheet loans; the loan book fell 21.9% to RMB4.3bn; and VAS revenue fell to RMB369M from RMB491M. A further rise in NPLs or in provisions in Q3 would weigh on earnings quality. VAS is about 11% of revenue, and the 89% in freight matching grew 9.6% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 NPL rise came with a -6% open and a -1.1% close; the effect of this line cannot be separated from the rest of that print.
findings.why_not_priced: This was disclosed in August, so it is mostly priced. What remains is whether Q3 shows a further step up. The segment is small net of the rest of the company.
findings.independence: Panabee's Q2 write-up flags the same risk (https://www.panabee.com/news/full-truck-alliance-earnings-q2-2026), but it reads the same release, so there is no independent source.

findings.finding: There is room in the FY2026 capital-return target. The board targets US$400M of returns in FY2026, at least US$300M through dividends. The quarterly dividend runs at about US$87.5M (US$0.084 per ADS), and the board may adjust dividends to reach about US$400M, so a Q4 dividend or buyback that tops up the year is likely to be declared with this print. Cash was RMB33.4bn (about US$4.9bn) against a market cap of roughly US$8-9bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The return plan announced on 2026-01-19 was credited with a rally on 2026-04-30 (+3.85%, rallies.ai). The Q1 2026 print with its dividend declaration closed +4.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The plan is public, so the Q4 top-up is expected. Only an upside surprise (a larger buyback or an early FY2027 plan) would move the stock, and that is not dated inside the window.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 release states the US$87.5M dividend and the US$400M target (https://finviz.com/news/383529/full-truck-alliance-co-ltd-announces-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results).

outside_window.finding: A FY2027 shareholder-return plan. Last year's plan was announced on 2026-01-19, separately from any print, and it requires at least 50% of the prior year's non-GAAP net income. With FY2026 adjusted net income likely above RMB5bn, the FY2027 floor is about US$370M or more. Its likely timing is January 2027.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no option chain and no reaction history, so the only priced statement is a mild drift lower (5d -4.4%, 29% off the high). The negative lean in the findings agrees with that drift, and the positive revenue-beat finding cuts against it but is damped by this name's record of not paying for revenue beats.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the revenue-beat finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.5, because Q2 2026's +6.7% over the top of the guide closed -1.1% and Q3 2025's revenue beat closed -11.9%.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a proxy): the diesel finding was cut from -1.0 to -0.8 and the road-freight finding from -0.7 to -0.5. Both stay filed.

Lesson 6: the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources, so there is no cap. Lessons 7 and 8 changed nothing: short interest is low and there is no confirmed unpriced company-level number.
